title: Wet season and dry season: seasons near the equator
examples: Why do some countries have a wet and a dry season?

figure.name: x-compare
figure.verdict: Near the equator, rain decides the seasons

explain.say: Ask a child in Kenya or Indonesia if they have winter, and they might say: we have the rains! Near the equator, the middle belt of the Earth, it is warm all year. So the seasons are about rain, not cold. Look at the two seasons side by side.

draw.text: Wet season and dry season: seasons near the equator

draw.name: x-compare

explain.say: See the Wet season lighting up? For a few months, heavy rain falls most days. In India it is called the monsoon, a season of strong rainy winds. Rivers fill, farmers plant rice and millet, and everything turns green. Have you ever been caught in a huge downpour?

draw.name: x-compare
draw.verdict: Near the equator, rain decides the seasons

explain.say: Now the Dry season glows. Little or no rain falls for months. Rivers shrink, the grass turns brown, and in Nigeria a dusty wind called the harmattan blows. Farmers harvest and store food. Why do you think animals walk far to find water?

draw.name: x-compare
draw.verdict: Near the equator, rain decides the seasons

explain.say: Far from the equator, in places like the UK, Japan or Canada, there are four seasons instead. See Winter light up: short, cold days, sometimes with snow. Which season are you in today?

stages.label: Summer
stages.ask: Why is it summer in Australia when it is winter in the UK?

explain.say: Then spring, summer and autumn come round again in a circle. Well done, season explorer! Wow fact: when it is summer in the UK, it is winter in Australia, so people there can have a barbecue on the beach at Christmas!

faq.q: Why do some countries have a wet and a dry season?
faq.a: Near the equator it is warm all year, but the bands of rainy winds and clouds move north and south during the year. When they pass over, it is the wet season; when they move away, it is the dry season.
asks: Why does it rain only in some months?

faq.a: A monsoon is a seasonal wind that brings months of heavy rain, especially in South Asia. In India the summer monsoon usually lasts from about June to September.
No. Countries near the equator, like Kenya, Indonesia and Brazil's Amazon region, are warm all year and have wet and dry seasons instead. Countries further away have a cold winter.
asks: Is there winter near the equator?

faq.q: Why is it summer in Australia when it is winter in the UK?
faq.a: The Earth is tilted. When the northern half leans towards the Sun, it has summer and the southern half has winter. Six months later it swaps.
asks: Why are the seasons opposite in the south?

faq.a: The harmattan is a dry, dusty wind that blows from the Sahara over West Africa, including Nigeria and Ghana, during the dry season, roughly from November to March.
asks: What is the dusty wind in Nigeria?

facts: India's south-west monsoon usually brings most of its rain between June and September.
The seasons in the northern and southern hemispheres are opposite because of Earth's tilt.

quiz.say: Near the equator, what usually decides the seasons?
quiz.show: Near the equator, seasons depend on…
quiz.why: It is warm all year near the equator, so the seasons are wet or dry.

wrong.1: It rarely snows near the equator, except on very high mountains.
wrong.2: Falling leaves mark autumn in places far from the equator.

quiz.say: It is July and summer in Japan. What season is it in Australia?
quiz.why: The seasons are opposite in the southern half of the world, so July is winter in Australia.

wrong.0: Australia's summer comes in December to February.
wrong.2: Spring in Australia is September to November.
